Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@clearretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form - governing law / emergency relief

Hi Monica,

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form redlines. Legal has a couple of non-starters we need to flag early so we can keep the procurement timeline moving. Their position:

- Governing law should be New York law (they prefer a familiar commercial bench).
- Jurisdiction: exclusive state and federal courts in New York for any disputes.
- No carveout for equitable relief to be litigated outside NY — they want to reserve that forum.

We understand Redwood has standard language that allows for injunctive relief in other venues; can you tell me whether Redwood would consider limiting that to immediate injunctive relief only, with a short notice/fix window? ClearRetail is sensitive to having a predictable forum.

I've attached the Redlines_Customer.docx with our markup. We're hoping to get to a mutually acceptable draft by end of week so procurement can issue PO.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Senior Counsel, ClearRetail

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form - governing law / emergency relief

Alex —

Appreciate the quick read. We're committed to keeping the procurement timeline intact. Looping in our GC team (cc'd) to propose a workable compromise. At a high level, Redwood's negotiating position is:

- We prefer California law for consistency across accounts; not a blocker but important operationally.
- Monetary disputes can go to arbitration (to limit cost and multijurisdictional litigation).
- We will accept a narrowly tailored equitable relief carveout that allows either party to seek injunctive relief in a court with jurisdiction over the defendant or where the infringement is occurring (we want this to be limited and not a blanket right to sue anywhere).

Can you confirm whether ClearRetail would accept: (i) California choice of law; (ii) arbitration for monetary claims with AAA/ICDR rules and seat in San Francisco; (iii) an express, narrow injunctive relief carveout permitting temporary injunctive relief in either party's local courts until arbitration proceeds? That combination often resolves forum predictability concerns while preserving emergency remedies.

If you can reply with a concrete proposal on those three items, we can evaluate and aim to finalize by end of week so procurement can issue the PO.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
